crop.notes: First column of page 8, 'Mangled McCoole (Continued from Fifth Page)': the handshake and rounds one to seven, ending mid-sentence at 'Thus ended at once the most and the least re-'. The rest, including 'After the Battle' about Allen's place, is in the second column and not in the clipping.

title.suggested: Round by round: Allen beats McCoole in seven rounds

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican gave a round-by-round account of Tom Allen's victory over Mike McCoole, ending in the seventh round when McCoole's second Tom Kelly threw up the sponge as Allen taunted the badly cut McCoole.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, Wednesday, Septe[mber] 24, 1873'. Not the St. Louis Republic (from 1888).

facts.fact: Allen beat Mike McCoole in seven rounds on September 23, 1873, with Jack Looney as referee; McCoole's second Tom Kelly threw up the sponge
In the sixth round Allen told McCoole it was their last fight
facts.quote: This is our last fight, Mike.

facts.fact: In the seventh round Allen asked McCoole's second Tom Kelly to stop the fight
facts.quote: Tom, it's a bloody shame to put such a man as this up before me. Take him out of the ring. I don't want to punish him any more.

notes: The current title and summary ('Tom Allen's Saloon and Concert Hall') come from the 'After the Battle' section in the second column, which is outside the clipping; the clipping is the fight itself. Continuation of article 467. McCoole wore emerald colors, Allen a blue sash with white spots.
